caption:
The 1% rule is dead. Here's what replaced it.

Old rule: rent should be 1% of the price every month. A $300K house → $3,000/mo.

In a lot of markets that house rents for ~$2,000. And the rule ignores the things that decide whether you make money: your rate, insurance, taxes, repairs.

What replaced it: real monthly cash flow.
Rent $2,000
− Mortgage $1,497 ($225K loan, 7%, 30 yr)
− Taxes + insurance $450
− Repairs/vacancy/CapEx $300
= −$247/mo

Break-even price on the same house ≈ $250K. The rule isn't the problem. The price is.

Example numbers for illustration only. Your market, rate and costs will differ.
